subject.title: [Feature]: System prompt architecture refactor — from fragmented rules to unified cognitive framework

question: Should OpenClaw keep its core prompt provider-neutral and optimize measured operational sections, or sponsor a universal cognitive-methodology redesign across providers?
rationale: This determines default reasoning behavior and the division of safety, channel, and runtime contracts between prompt and code for every user; repository evidence cannot resolve that product policy automatically.

options.title: Measured section reductions
options.body: Retain the contract-oriented core prompt and incrementally shrink or dynamically scope sections after controlled prompt-budget and task-quality evaluation.

options.title: Cognitive framework program
options.body: Sponsor a staged RFC and benchmark effort for a universal default methodology plus equivalent runtime enforcement for removed contracts.

options.title: External methodology only
options.body: Keep cognitive methodology in provider overlays, skills, and user prompts and accept only independent prompt bugs or proven token optimizations in core.

recommendation.title: Measured section reductions
recommendation.body: Retain the contract-oriented core prompt and incrementally shrink or dynamically scope sections after controlled prompt-budget and task-quality evaluation.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior prompt review identifies this handle for product direction, and current-main history gives the strongest ownership signal for the central prompt surface.
